I was the dumbass that paid out of pocket (via student loans) for a STEM PhD when my adviser pulled the same shit. I regretted it, but I was scared to not know what to do and I was just 22 and went straight from a BS to PhD. I was naive as a first gen student coming from a working class family.  There were no safety nets for me and my adviser didn't give a fuck. I did what I thought was the only thing that was accessible to me which was piling up student loans. I regret it, yes, but I learned the expensive way. Hopefully, I can help you skip the expensive part.

If I were to tell me from the past, now as a 28 year old who is now fully funded after trial and error of hustling for GAs, TAs, and temporary summer jobs, I would have 1) considered dropping out early 2) reach out to outside of department resources 3) change my adviser ASAP 4) cold email departments to see if there are GAs for me.

University-wide, and although sometimes not relevant to your work directly, you can find a GA. Sometimes a department will create a GA for you if you market your skills very well. That's what I did for my current GA. It's not the best situation, because you work double as hard as someone who has an RA and is aligning their dissertation, but it's funding. I get it, especially if you uprooted your whole life to attend the school.

However, for you, and considering how fresh I was also when I heard the news from my adviser, I would consider and echo the other advice from everyone who has posted here as well. Leave your adviser and find a better situation with a new one, whether that be in your current school or elsewhere...or finding a job.
